original_poem:
கண்ணனின் வாசல்,  
உன் செந்நெல் போல,  
என் கண்ணில் பொன் நிறம்,  
காதலின் கனி ஆகின்றது!
translated_poem:
The entrance of Krishna,  
Like your golden paddy,  
In my eyes, the hue of gold,  
Becomes the fruit of love!

stanzas.loss_note: செந்நெல் (chennel) is not merely 'golden paddy' but the red-husked paddy of Tamil agrarian ritual, carrying Pongal-harvest covenant resonance; the comparison of Krishna's threshold to ripening paddy invokes the akam tinai of marutham (fertile riverine landscape) which the translation flattens into a generic colour simile.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the ripening of devotion as harvest abundance at the beloved deity's threshold
love reaching its fullest, sweetest culmination like fruit at the moment of harvest

cultural_entities.translation_note: கண்ணன் (Kannan) is the Tamil name for Krishna, carrying the Alvar bhakti tradition's intimate address; 'Krishna' in translation preserves the deity but loses the Tamil devotional register of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
Rendered as 'golden paddy' — chennel is the red-husked paddy of Tamil agrarian ritual, specifically associated with Pongal offerings and the marutham tinai landscape.
